advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Only warn in `_normalize_transition_force` when a boolean `force` is truthy (or otherwise word the warning so `force=False` is not told the `force=True` surface is deprecated).
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:247: `if isinstance(force, bool):`
src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:248: `warn_deprecated("lib:rebar.transition(force=True)", via="warning")`
src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:249: `result = "(no reason given)" if force else None`
The registry name used to build the message is `rebar.transition(force=True)` (src/rebar/_deprecations.py:101), so a `force=False` caller is told the `force=True` surface is deprecated.
advisory.finding: `_normalize_transition_force` emits a `DeprecationWarning` for the benign no-op `force=False` (the previously-default boolean spelling), and the warning's registered surface text is `rebar.transition(force=True)` — misleading for a caller who explicitly passed `False` and never intended to force anything.
scenarios: A library caller that historically wrote `transition(..., force=False)` explicitly (the old default value) now receives a DeprecationWarning referencing `force=True` on a call that does not force.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard the warning on the value: `if isinstance(force, bool):` then `result = None if not force else "(no reason given)"`; only call `warn_deprecated(...)` when `force is True` (a `force=False` no-op need not warn), or reword the registered name to cover the boolean spelling generally.
